story: At 7:17 on a sunny Tuesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his workbench in his own house, soldering speaker wiring and testing his light strings indoors with the golf cart left alone in the driveway. Down the street, Donna is at her kitchen table with the club calendar, hoping to pencil in a doubles practice with Gary once she finds an open court. Over at his house, Hal is flipping through his violation notebook, determined to record only what the community rules actually cover, while Rosa sits content with her shift schedule for the week ahead.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Finish soldering the speaker wiring and test the light strings indoors, cart untouched
Donna (donna club calendar): Check open court times and pencil in a doubles practice with Gary
Hal (hal violation notebook): Review my entries on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos, and note only what the rules actually cover
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Check my per-diem shift schedule for the week

gary.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM and I'm home alone. I filed the modification form at the Architectural Review desk back at ticks 35 and 36, and I've been bench-testing everything indoors so the cart stays untouched, which keeps me honest with L-01. Quiet hours ended at 7 AM, so some speaker testing is fine now, but low volume is still the neighborly way. The sound system wiring isn't finished, and I can keep working on it at the bench without breaking any rule. Staying busy beats rattling around an empty house, and the parade is coming up.

parameters.content: Finish soldering the speaker wiring and test the light strings indoors, cart untouched

donna.thought_process: It's a sunny Tuesday morning and I'm home alone. Last night's dinner at Rosa's is behind us, but Gary and I are on the ladder now and I haven't heard from him since he wandered off. Nobody is nearby to talk to, so the useful thing is to run the club side of this: check my calendar for open court slots (staying inside the two-hour reservation limit) so I can lock in a practice time with Gary and keep us climbing.

parameters.content: Check open court times and pencil in a doubles practice with Gary

hal.thought_process: Morning after Rosa's dinner. Apology made, platter carried, and I'm home with nobody in sight. My notebook is still sitting here, and the flamingo count and Gary's cart mods are still unreported. But the reflection nags at me: I'm keeping a ledger of everyone's mistakes. Rules are rules, though, and I can follow them without being a scold. I'll check the notebook and get the entries straight, so that anything I file at Town Hall is accurate, specific, and fair, not petty.

parameters.content: Review my entries on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos, and note only what the rules actually cover

rosa.thought_process: It's 7:17 on a Tuesday morning and the big dinner has already happened. Everyone pitched in at the table, Hal carried the platter, Donna set out napkins, and I finally got the three of them around one table. Nobody's nearby, and my goal is basically met. I'm still an overcommitted per-diem nurse, so the sensible thing is to check my shift schedule and see what my week looks like now that the hosting is done.

parameters.content: Check my per-diem shift schedule for the week

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
